narrative.overview:
This is a portfolio where seniority is implied, never announced. The dark surface absorbs light and attention without reflecting it back — it exists to hold the work forward, not to perform confidence on its own behalf. Every element that remains has earned its place; everything decorative has been removed. The result is a surface that reads as premium the same way a well-machined tool does: through precision and the absence of excess.

The color strategy is restrained: a single cool blue-violet accent carries less than 10% of any surface. It appears on exactly the actions and moments that deserve weight — the call-to-action button, the work timeline thread. Its restraint is the point. If the accent is everywhere, it is nowhere.

The register is brand. The portfolio itself is the proof of engineering judgment. A designer looking at this interface should be unable to pin the aesthetic to a generic category. It is not dark-mode SaaS cream. It is not cyberpunk. It is not a formatted white CV. It is a built object that demonstrates the same taste its owner applies to production code.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: designed for dark mode, adapted for light
Single accent: cool blue-violet, strictly rationed
Flat surfaces with tonal depth — no shadow theater
Two-family system: Schibsted Grotesk for structure (name, section headers, group labels), Inter for content. Hierarchy through scale, weight, and family role.
One personality beat: the sprite cursor follower. No more.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The Accent Violet appears on ≤10% of any given surface. It is a voice, not a wallpaper. Using it on two things simultaneously dilutes both.

rules.name: The Neutral Tint Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries chroma 0.005–0.035 toward hue 260–268. Pure gray neutrals are prohibited; they flatten the surface and read as uncurated defaults.

rules.name: The Role-Split Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk is for structure (identity, section headers, group labels); Inter is for content. Never use the display face for body prose, and never reach for a third family. No decorative serifs, no monospace 'developer' accents. The scale carries hierarchy at a ≥1.25 ratio between steps — no flat scales.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No surface casts a shadow at rest. Shadows are reserved for hover states on interactive cards. If adding a shadow to a new component, first ask whether the component truly needs to communicate lift.

rules.name: The One Personality Beat Rule
rules.body: The sprite cursor follower is the single moment of playfulness the system allows. Resist all other motion, delight, or decorative additions. Its scarcity is what makes it memorable.

rules.name: The Neutral Chip Rule
rules.body: Chips are never color-coded. Tier is carried by fill (solid chip-core vs transparent outline), not hue. The group heading names the category, the fill names the proficiency tier, and color stays rationed to the violet accent. Outline chips keep full-contrast text-primary so the demotion never costs legibility (WCAG AA).

dos: Do use accent-violet (oklch(0.55 0.19 268)) as the accent — a cooler, more considered blue-violet than the previous purple-600. Update legacy purple-600 usages as surfaces are touched.
Do keep every neutral surface tilted toward hue 260–268, even at near-zero chroma. Pure grays are prohibited.
Do use tonal surface steps (ink-well → surface-elevated → surface-secondary) as the depth model. Shadows are hover-only.
Do use Schibsted Grotesk for structural type (name, section headers, group labels) and Inter for content. Let the role split and weight carry hierarchy.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: the sprite component must be hidden under reduced-motion preferences.
Do keep line length to 65–75ch in body prose sections (About, work descriptions).
Do keep skill chips neutral. The group heading names the category; tier is carried by fill (solid chip-core vs outline), and color on chips is redundant and steals from the accent.
donts: Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe. The current border-l-2 border-purple-500 on work entries is a legacy pattern to replace.
Don't make this look like a generic shadcn/Tailwind default theme.
Don't use dark mode with purple gradients, neon accents, or glassmorphism.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient fill).
Don't design a white CV with no visual intent in light mode.
Don't add ambient glow effects, animated gradient backgrounds, or particle systems.
Don't use the accent color on more than one interactive element per visible screen area.

Don't reintroduce per-category badge colors, and don't carry the core/secondary tier with color either. Tier is fill (solid vs outline); color belongs to the single violet accent, not the skill taxonomy.
